Subject: Pilot: short extension and credit-topup options

Hi Olga / Marissa,

Quick ask from our side — we've hit a heavier ingestion window on the POC (batching larger files) and need an extra two weeks to finish our final throughput and cost-per-token validation. Our procurement team prefers not to take a long-term commitment yet; would you be able to either

- extend the pilot by 14 days, or
- sell a modest top-up of runtime credits we can consume during the extra testing?

If we go the credit route, we'd prefer invoicing (net 30) to avoid an upfront PO amendment. Also, are there any limits if we switch to a Dedicated trial node briefly for throughput testing? We only need it for 24–48 hours during the new window.

Happy to jump on a quick call this afternoon if that's easier.

Thanks,

Head of ML Ops
BlueMesa Analytics

Hi Maria — thanks for the note and context. We can accommodate either approach; below are two pragmatic paths we typically offer for time-boxed evaluations:

Option A — 14-day time extension (no invoice change)
- Quick addendum to the existing pilot: extends end date by 14 days.
- No incremental cost if usage stays within the original token cap.
- If usage exceeds cap, those overage tokens billed at the pilot rate (see attached pricing sheet).

Option B — Credit top-up (preferred by procurement)
- One-off top-up: 50k token credit pack at a discounted pilot rate ($0.00018/token => $9.00 estimate).
- We issue an invoice (net 30) for the credit pack; credits consumed during the two-week window.
- Top-up avoids changing the pilot contract dates.

Dedicated short-burst (24–48 hrs)
- We can provision a Dedicated node for a short window; engineering needs a 48-hour lead time to reserve capacity. There is a burst fee ($300/day) to cover reservation and priority routing. If you convert to Dedicated within 60 days we can apply the burst fee as credit toward the first month.

I attached the current pricing summary and a draft SOW for the addendum so legal/procurement have something to review. If you prefer, I can draft the addendum language today and loop in Legal. What does procurement prefer for invoicing (PO vs invoice to procurement@blu emesa.ai)?

Next steps proposed:
- You confirm which option (A or B) and whether you want the Dedicated 48-hr test.
- If Option B, I’ll create an invoice and send a short DocuSign addendum for signatures.

Cheers,
Olga Petrov
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
olga@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198

Maria — quick add from the commercial side. We want to make this low friction for you while still keeping conversion levers aligned:

- If you pick Option A (pure extension), Redwood will add a one-time 20% pilot discount on any overage tokens during the extension period, provided BlueMesa signs a conversion commitment within 45 days after the pilot end.
- If you pick Option B (credit top-up + invoice), we can offer a 15% discount on the credit pack (procurement-friendly invoicing) instead of the 20% conversion discount. The slightly smaller discount reflects the different commercial treatment and billing mechanics.

Ben — can you confirm engineering lead time on the Dedicated 48-hr spike and whether burst fee can be credited back on conversion?

Marissa Cole
